Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge (priming assay)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TNF, EGF, or PMA), let it wash out for hours to days, then re-stimulate and measure transcription of AP-1 target genes by RNA-seq and nascent RNA (PRO-seq). Like the 'compass that bends' and is echoed later, a faster or stronger second response, lost when AP-1 is inhibited, would show a memory that depends on AP-1. Compare naive, primed, and AP-1-depleted cells.

ideas.title: Longitudinal chromatin accessibility and AP-1 occupancy tracking
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN family members, and H3K27ac ChIP at time points before, during and long after the stimulus. Look for enhancers that stay open and AP-1-bound after the signal has gone, as if a 'mended atlas' retained a trace. Motif footprinting would show whether AP-1 binding persists or whether it only leaves behind an epigenetic mark.

ideas.title: Acute degron perturbation at defined memory phases
ideas.description: Fuse AP-1 subunits (c-JUN, FOSL1, or a dominant-negative like A-FOS) to a degron or place them under inducible control. Remove AP-1 either only during the initial stimulus (testing for establishment) or only after the stimulus ends (testing for maintenance), then re-challenge the cells. This separates AP-1 as a writer of memory from AP-1 as a maintainer, and it controls for the cells' general responsiveness.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 reporters with lineage tracking
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN or a fluorescent AP-1 transcriptional reporter in single cells across stimulation, rest, and re-stimulation, and follow daughter cells through divisions. Measure whether activity states persist, are heritable, and are bistable, using autocorrelation between mother and daughter cells. Fit the data to a mathematical model of positive feedback (JUN autoregulation) to test whether the memory is a cell-intrinsic state.

ideas.title: Targeted epigenome editing of AP-1 sites to test sufficiency and necessity
ideas.description: Use dCas9-based tools (KRAB or p300) or motif mutations through CRISPR base editing to alter specific AP-1-bound enhancers that stay accessible after the signal. Test whether closing them erases the primed response, and whether forced AP-1 binding or opening creates a memory without the stimulus. Readouts are the gene expression response to re-challenge and the persistence of chromatin marks, which would show causality at single loci.
